title: Check whether the published scribe prediction disagreements survive train-fitted IDF
statement: Verified the three public file hashes, all 93 balanced page labels, and the seven unanimous alternate trigram labels. On f55r all four classifiers also disagree with the published label but give two distinct alternatives. The saved notebook's bigram run scores 82 and 70 for SVM and the tree, versus 79 and 61 in the CSV. The original fold assignment and random states are unavailable. On 20 matched reconstructed trigram splits, switching only test IDF changes 14/1860 Naive Bayes, 26/1860 linear SVM, and 38/1860 tree predictions, covering 4, 10 and 24 different pages respectively. The mean correct count rises by 0.40, 0.40 and 0.10 pages per 93. Trigram predictions for the two-token f116v do not change in any comparison. A labelled supplementary NumPy DNN reconstruction changes 36/1860 predictions. The count-based TF-IDF reconstruction matches the vectorizer matrices for all 20 checked folds. The seven classifier inputs map to 13 Yale panels. In a same-layout blind pilot, two readers locate all eight interior o exemplars in each of f85r1 and f86v5. Both see zero definite neighboring attachments in f85r1 and see five and six respectively in f86v5. They agree on closure for 15/16 glyphs and on attachment or uncertainty for 12/16. This local two-panel sample supports an attachment contrast that can be tested against more sections and more hands. The f116v crop shows two words in one eligible locus and is below the three-locus floor.
check: Recompute paired changes from the stored seed, fold indices and prediction strings. For a more independent test group panels by their physical leaf and quire, balance script context and layout within each tested hand, and prespecify training-only preprocessing. Across independently allocated panel pairs, use the same matching rules for EVA o and at least one other glyph, include adequate negative controls, and preserve disagreement. Estimate effect of known Currier and layout groupings separately from reported scribe labels. Keep the short f116v marginal text below the three-locus minimum unless another independently supported locus is found.
protocol:
# P-L1-026 paired IDF reconstruction

Verify the three public files against the published audit SHA-256 values.
Read the notebook as text. Reimplement its prefix grouping, CP1252 decoding,
ambiguous-token removal, shortest-page pruning of scribes 1 and 2, and
retention of all scribe 3 pages. Compare the exact 93 page and scribe pairs
and seven unanimous disagreements to the public CSV. Compute separate
panel and retained token counts. Record distinctions between the displayed
notebook run and final CSV. Do not infer unavailable author seeds or folds.

Reconstruct unstratified 10-fold KFold with shuffle=True for fixed seeds
2860–2879. Use the same page order and folds for bigrams and trigrams.
For each scribe and fold, cut off nominal counts at 50 on the joined
training strings to derive max_features, refit the character vectorizer
to that scribe's separate training pages as in the source, and take the
union. Use a sorted union for reproducible feature column order. Preserve
the training vocabulary, L2 normalization and min/max in both arms.

Fit training vocabulary, TF-IDF and the common models once per fold.
For the notebook arm, construct the test matrix with a second fit using
only the test texts and the fixed training vocabulary. For the corrected
arm, transform test texts with the training IDF. Per fold record vocabulary
size and hash, per-scribe cutoffs, number and extent of differing IDFs,
page indices and any zero feature spans. Share fitted models and pair
predictions. The three classical models use the released forms (default
MultinomialNB, linear SVC and default tree settings with explicit seed).
For a labelled supplementary reconstruction, approximate the published
Dense architecture in NumPy with three ReLU layers of width M, M, floor(M/2),
M=floor((number_of_features+3)/2), three-way softmax, Glorot uniform kernel,
zero biases, five epochs, shuffled batches of 32, Adam learning rate .001
and beta .9/.999 with epsilon 1e-7. This implementation and its seeded
fits differ from the unseeded Keras notebook run.

Compare within-run differences in accuracy and predicted class, record
switches to/from the published label, and give per-page results for all
93 records and the seven highlighted rows. Repeated seeds reuse the
same inputs; report descriptive variation and avoid treating shared
manuscript text or folds as independent new evidence about scribes.
visual_protocol:
# Running-prose visual eligibility plan

Fix f85r1 and f86v5 before measuring features. Each is a text-only pane
of quire 14, with a standard left-to-right paragraph at the top. Compare
the first four physical paragraph loci from each panel. The assignment
to anonymous image packs is kept out of the scorer's instructions.
Neither panel serves as an independently known hand identity.

Primary glyph is the ordinary single EVA-basic 'o'. Eligible tokens
are legible, contain no uncertain or rare-glyph markers, are not first
or last in their line, and have o strictly before the final and after
the initial glyph of the token. Exclude glyphs touching adjacent lines,
crease damage, and visually inseparable groups. Enough evidence
requires at least eight eligible o exemplars from distinct words across
at least three original paragraph loci on both sides. Sampling keeps
the first qualifying occurrence per word when there are repeats.
Track preceding q vs other separately. Preserve a window of the original
line for local baselines and pixel-scale evidence. For a direct shape
comparison record oval closure, an ascender or descender attachment and
any ambiguity. Two independent readers use the same anonymized crops,
cannot see paper classes or predictions, and report counts and
disagreements without assigning a hand.

For f116v the ZL record has one Voynich locus and two words. Adjacent
extraneous writing is out of scope, so this panel cannot meet the
three-locus support rule. Save its actual registration crop as evidence.

historical_counts.interpretation: The notebook reports its all-sample counts with >50 and chooses per-scribe fold feature caps with >=50.

notes.matrix_validation: Count-vectorizer smoothing formula, L2 normalization and the training min/max give the same matrices to 1e-12, with fixed seed 2860, both n-gram lengths, all 10 folds.
notes.minmax: Original and paired corrected test features remain un-clipped after train min/max; test values below the train minimum are kept and counted.
notes.prediction_codes: Each string has one character per row in evidence.pages; 1, 2 and 3 denote the corresponding published scribe class.

concentric_circular_text.condition: Use only text on circular baselines of like radial curvature after rotation to common tangent; keep isolated labels outside this comparison.

plant_interrupted_paragraph.condition: Use only line fragments on the same side of a plant interruption, matching line and word position. f94v is left of f95r1 on canvas 1006241 and keeps layout and quire close. f4v is a separate-quire comparison sharing interrupted lines.

running_prose.condition: Use paragraph interiors with left-to-right horizontal baselines and exclude stars, marginal marks and line edges. f85r1 and f86v5 form the frozen within-quire pair, not two independent books or a known hand split.

rotated_floating_paragraphs.condition: Compare matched compass blocks only with baselines rotated to upright. The two panels supply within-quire comparisons. An independent equal-layout control has not been verified.

above_plant_paragraphs.condition: Keep ordinary above-plant paragraphs separate from wrapping lines. The matched controls should be chosen before reading.

f116v_eligibility.decision: Insufficient. Exclude neighboring non-Voynich writing and do not infer a hand.

anonymous_reader_a.coordinate_system: Approximate [left, top, right, bottom] in original panel pixels, from the upper-left origin. The right and bottom bounds are exclusive.
anonymous_reader_a.method: Matched the guide word order to each original panel and inspected enlarged color and contrast-adjusted grayscale views. Attachment denotes visible ink contact with either neighboring glyph. Unclear marks an ambiguous stroke contact or closure.
